body.title: Run the hooks from executeTool
body.summary: Route executeTool's two success exits through one helper that calls runToolHooks with the resolved tool, and sets hookFailures and appends one `[hook failed] <hookId>: <message>` line per failure to output only when a rule failed; every failed exit stays hook-free and a call with no hook returns the very object the tool returned. Extend tool-hooks.test.ts with the executor tests.
acceptanceChecks: a registered rule runs once after a successful call for caller agent, daemon, workflow and unset, with and without an outputSchema
a failed, denied, rejected or schema-mismatch call runs no rule and carries no hookFailures
a tool called through an alias runs the canonical id's hooks exactly once
a failing rule leaves success, data and format unchanged, sets hookFailures, and appends exactly one `[hook failed] <hookId>: <message>` line per failure to output
hookFailures is absent when no rule failed and the result object is the one the tool returned when no hook is registered

tests.name: src/daemon/tools/__tests__/tool-hooks.test.ts: a registered rule runs once after a successful call for each caller (agent, daemon, workflow, unset)
src/daemon/tools/__tests__/tool-hooks.test.ts: a tool with no outputSchema still runs its rules
src/daemon/tools/__tests__/tool-hooks.test.ts: a tool called through an alias runs the canonical id's rule exactly once
src/daemon/tools/__tests__/tool-hooks.test.ts: a failing rule leaves the result a success and reports the failure on hookFailures and in the output text
src/daemon/tools/__tests__/tool-hooks.test.ts: a failed, denied, rejected or schema-mismatch call runs no rule
src/daemon/tools/__tests__/tool-hooks.test.ts: rules run in registration order and a failing rule does not stop the next
src/daemon/tools/__tests__/tool-hooks.test.ts: a call with no rule returns the object the tool returned
